He is an active fighter in our communalist field.
He supports taking over state palaces and hotels in order to house the poor.
Like Abd al-Qadir al-Jili, he believes that “the comfort of creation” is the root of everything.
He wants to take possession of Iraq so that he can distribute it among its hungry.
He lives by the work of his own hands.
Others drink from cups filled to the brim with wine.
My own cup holds labyrinths and grief.
Tired eyelids find their rest in sleep.
My eyes find rest in the company of stars.
If only my cares were like other people’s:
My heart melts among them though they have hardened,
as a lamp melts in the depth of night.
I almost weep for them whenever they laugh.
I almost laugh at them whenever they mourn.
Against the wind, by some enchantment, without a compass,
I travel where there are no ships and no sailor.
Alone amid the uproar of night, forever silent:
When will the night give way to dawn?
I am the stranger with a wound
that union with the beloved cannot quiet
Today I received a card from him for the birthday of Jesus.
My sorrow and pain—not congratulations and not joy—on the birthday of our teacher, which the world celebrates by crucifying him all over again.
What can a grieving lover like me offer on this yearly catastrophe except flowers draped in black and steeped in tears?
His birth has been turned into an annual death of the spirit, an excuse for more profit in trade and more pleasure for the body.
Forgive my madness and the strange rhythm in which I move.
I have nothing to console me in what I am going through except my cup, which I drank to the voice of the Beloved.
I have not sobered from its wine, the wine that set me alight in this frozen world around me.
And while I was drunk, our teacher called to me and made me weep.
“What reward is there in loving someone who loves you?”
“In him I have gathered all humanity, because he alone is still alive among these graves.”
Then he wept, and the light around me disappeared…
Drunken one, grow still more awake through drunkenness.
Buy the cup with everything you own in this world,
and gain through it honour and splendour.
Discover in the wine the meaning within you that reason lost.
Reach the depth that revealed itself in you and reached its furthest point.
and see the light enthroned within you as God.
Merge into its spirit through love,
for you are nothing but that spirit.
Lose yourself in Him through Him:
so that silence might grow lips through you;
so that you might hold water inside stone for the trees;
so that you might clothe a bird in safety and in dreams.
Be nothing but what you choose to be,
in your own choosing and your own direction.
Beneath the pearls of night in my master’s garden,
All the gazelles of the earth gathered
tracing tiny patterns from mysterious letters
The rose tore open its clothes.
I broke every jar of wine.
You prolong Your coyness in me.
and I became like someone imprisoned
The morning stars disappear quickly before the face of the sun,
for the life of a star is limited.
And even to the one who is certain of the sun,
the life of the sun is limited.
whoever seeks some possession on the earth will find it.
The deprived questioner is the one who asks about something and receives no answer.
Certainty is a sultan who sees heresy in negation.
And sultans, when you fail to understand them,
So walk the roads of estrangement.
Do not submit to any depth.
Do not search for some distant end stored away in the Tablet, and do not write with any eyelid but your own.
There is no human being at the bottom.
The circle of the sky grows narrow when it is filled with anything other than thought: thought burning with the fire of ecstasy, kindled in the lands of care and intimate whispering.
